texts.preamble: Ajay Kumar Gupta vs Delhi Admn/Food Inspector on 5 March, 2021 The Court Of Shri Anil Antil Additional Sessions Judge-04, New Delhi District Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Criminal Appeal Number : 8729/2016 Cc No. : 55/2005 U/S: : 16(1A) r/w Section 7 of P.F.A Act-1954 Ajay Kumar Gupta @ Ajay Kumar, s/o Sh. Om Prakash Gupta, R/o H.No. 109, Extension-III, Nangloi, Delhi-41. .....Appellant versus Delhi Admn/Food Inspector, Department of Pfa, Govt of Nt of Delhi, A-20, Lawrence Road, Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 .....Respondent Appeal received by Predecessor Court on: 07.09.2016 And By this court on : 13.08.2020 Arguments concluded : 05.03.2021
texts.facts: The complaint was then filed in the court on 07.03.2005 alleging violation of Section 2(ia),(j) and (m) of PFA Act r/w Rules 23, 28 & 29 of PFA Rules, as punishable under Section 7/16(1A) of PFA. Act. - that the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, hence, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with ; 4. The appellant/accused was summoned by the learned trial court vide order dated 07.03.2005 for 26.07.2005 to face trial. After filing appearance, accused filed an application under Section 13(2) of the PFA Act, thereby exercising right to get the second counterpart of the sample analyzed from the Central Food Ajay Kumar Gupta vs Delhi Admn/Food Inspector on 5 March, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189032825/ 2 Laboratory (CFL). The application was allowed and the counter part CA no. 8729/16 Ajay Kr. Gupta @ Ajay Kumar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) pages 3 of 13 was sent to the CFL ; director CFL examined the sample and gave his report vide certificate dated 30.04.2005 opining the sample to be not confirming to the standards of Rice as per PFA Rules due to presence of Synthetic Colours "Tartrazine" and "Sunset Yellow FCF". 5. Thereafter matter was listed for pre-charge evidence, wherein the complainant examined PW-1 Sh.Sanjeev Kumar Gupta, Food Inspector. 6. On the basis of testimony of prosecution witness (PW1) on 21.07.2008 charge was framed against the appellant/accused for commission of offences punishable u/s 7/16(1A) of PFA Act for violation of provisions of Sub clause 2(i)(ia)(j) of PFA Act alleging therein that on 16.12.2004 at about 05:15 p.m. appellant/ accused being the Vendor cum Proprietor of M/s Royal Caterers, Khasra No. 1012, Prem Nagar-II, Kirari, Delhi was found present at the given premises and conducting business of food article and sold for analysis sample of Sela Rice of approximately 1500 grams taken from an open small gunny bag having no label declaration which was meant for human consumption and it was analyzed by the Director CFL vide Certificate no. 63/LHA/10737 dated 30.04.2005 and found that the sample is adulterated as there was presence of synthetic colour i.e. tartrazine + Sunset yellow FCF and thereby violated the provisions of Section 2(i)(ia) (j) of PFA Act, 1954 punishable under section 16(1A) of PFA Act, 1954 read with Section 7 of the PFA Act to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 6.1 During trial after the examination and detailed cross CA no. 8729/16 Ajay Kr. Gupta @ Ajay Kumar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) pages 4 of 13 examination of three witnesses of the department i.e. PW-1 Sh. Sanjeev Kumar Gupta, Food Inspector, PW-2 Sh. Brahamanand, Field Assistant and PW-3 Sh. Harish Kumar Ahuja, the then Local Health Authority/SDM prosecution evidence was closed and matter was fixed for Statement of accused. 7. The statement of appellant/accused was recorded under section 313 Cr.PC in which he pleaded his innocence and stated that no efforts were made to join the public witnesses, no payment was made, sample was not mixed properly, jhaba was not made clean before using it ; the relevant documents were not read over or explained to him before obtaining his signatures ; PA and CFL reports are wrong ; no adulteration was made by him, it is a false case and he used to serve cooked food to the MCD School children and received money for the cooking of food from the MCD authorities and he prefer to lead DE but despite opportunity no witness was produced. 9.(I) The appellant has assailed the judgment and order on sentence passed by the learned trial court by urging various grounds.
texts.arguments: II) Alternatively, on the quantum of sentence, relying upon the new legislation, it was pleaded that the case of the appellant be considered sympathetically in the light of the preposition of law laid down by the Hon'ble Courts pursuant to coming of new legislation that is Food Safety & Standards Act. Learned counsel for the Delhi Admn./Food Department, objected to the same and submitted that according to submission of CA no. 8729/16 Ajay Kr. Gupta @ Ajay Kumar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) pages 6 of 13 appellant, prosecution has established its case and he be sentenced with strict punishment in terms of old Act wherein minimum punishment is prescribed and no leniency should be shown to the convict as it is a serious offence of food adulteration article / commodity leading to hazardous consequences on the health or body of a person. 12. 14. It is argued by learned counsel for the appellant that on the date of pronouncement of judgment/order on sentence, the PFA Act, 1954 was repealed and new act has thereafter come into operation. It is stated that the court should give benefit of the new legislation to the accused vide which the punishment provided under the old act has been diluted to a considerable extent, and that Ajay Kumar Gupta vs Delhi Admn/Food Inspector on 5 March, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189032825/ 4 the offence for which the accused/appellant has been convicted now falls under the CA no. 8729/16 Ajay Kr. Gupta @ Ajay Kumar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) pages 7 of 13 category of "Unsafe Food" punishable under section 59(1) of the new Act i.e Food and Safety Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter called FSSAI) punishable upto six months and fine of upto Rs. One lac only. 15. It was argued by learned counsel for the appellant that appellant is a man of 45 years of age, respectable person of society, has deep roots in the society, running a small Kiryana shop for livelihood of his family consisting of wife, one son and one daughter and old aged parents who are suffering from various old age ailments, has duties and responsibilities towards his family, not involved in any other case, and prayed that a lenient view be taken against him in the light of the provisions of law under the new Act. 15.1 Further it is stated that case pertains to the year 2004, the appellant/accused has faced the trial almost 17 years which by itself is a sufficient punishment and, the hardships faced by him has caused him great mental agony, stress and rigors of trial during the said period. It is also stated that now a days special circumstances exists due to outbreak of pandemic of Covid-19 and there are chances of appellant being infected with virus in case imprisonment of sentence is awarded to him. 15.2 In support of his submissions qua the consideration of the case under new legislation, learned counsel for appellant had relied upon the judgment of Nemi Chand Vs. State of Rajasthan ( Crl. Appeals No. 214 and 215 of 2016, vide order dated 10.03.2016, as corrected vide order dated 17.03.2016, as reported in 2016 (1) FAC 203 ) of Hon'ble Supreme Court and earlier judgment T Barai CA no. 8729/16 Ajay Kr. Gupta @ Ajay Kumar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) pages 8 of 13 Vs. Henry 1983 ( ) SCC 177. 15.3 Per contra, learned SPP, strongly opposed the submissions advanced by learned counsel by addressing that the sentencing cannot be done in new Act since the definition of many offences have changed in the new Act including this particular offence of which accused is charged. Definition of major offences like "adulteration" and "misbranding" have been changed. Now FSSAI have definition "substandard food", "food containing extraneous matter" "unsafe food" and misbranded food". - Sub-clause (viii) of 3(zz) FSSA Act is applicable where the colouring material or the preservative other than that specified in respect there of is found in the food article and not where the CA no. Ajay Kumar Gupta vs Delhi Admn/Food Inspector on 5 March, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189032825/ 5 8729/16 Ajay Kr. Gupta @ Ajay Kumar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) pages 9 of 13 colouring material exceeds the prescribed limit. 15.8 Now, coming to the application of Nemi Chand Judgment (supra), the same is based on the old judgment i.e. T Barai ( Supra) of Hon'ble Supreme Court. The relevant portion of the T Barai Judgment is as follows : - (Para 25) It is settled both on authority and principle that when a later statute again describes an offence created by an earlier statute and imposes a different punishment or varies the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by implication in Michell Vs. Brown ( 1958) 120 ER 909, 912 : 32 LTOS 146:7 WR 80 Lord Campbell put the matter thus : - "It is well settled rule of construction that, if a later statute again describes an ofence created by a former statute and affixes a different punishment, varying the procedure, the earlier statute is CA no. 8729/16 Ajay Kr. Gupta @ Ajay Kumar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) pages 10 of 13 repealed by the later statute see also Smith Vs. Benabo ( 1937) 1 ALL ER 523 : ( 1997) 1 KB 518: 156 LT 194" - In Regina Vs. Youle ( 1861) 158 ER 311,315-16 : LT 299 : 9 WR 637 Martin B. said in the oft-quoted passage : - If a statute deals with a particular class of offences, and a subsequent Act is passed which deals with precisely the same offence, and a different punishment is imposed by the later Act, I think that, in effect, the legislature has declared that the new Act shall be substituted for the earlier Act." - The rule is however subject to the limitation contained in Article 20(1) against ex post facto law providing for a greater punishment and has also no application where the offence described in the later Act is not the same as in the earlier Act i.e. when the essential ingredients of the two offences are different. - Moreover, this particular aspect is stated as a illustration in the same judgment in Para 23 which is as follows : Ajay Kumar Gupta vs Delhi Admn/Food Inspector on 5 March, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189032825/ 6 - To illustrate, if Parliament were to reenact Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and provide that the punishment for an offence of murder shall be sentence for imprisonment for life instead of the present sentence of death or imprisonment for life, then it can not be that the courts would still award a sentence of death even in pending cases. 15-A - Academic Reference can also be made to the letter dated 03.10.2017 of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, produced before the court during the proceedings. Vide said letter the said authority, in the light of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court CA no. 8729/16 Ajay Kr. Gupta @ Ajay Kumar Vs. Food Inspector (PFA) pages 11 of 13 in Nemi Chand's Case (supra) issued an advisory to the Commissioners of Food Safety/Officers incharge of Food Safety to dispose of the long pending court cases filed under old PFA Act mainly concerning substandard and misbranding by imposing fine only.
